property.text: The hash input order in compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge (SG-006) MUST be deterministic and canonical across all client implementations. All clients MUST serialize fields in the identical order: domain, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL, len(commitments), len(cell_indices), commitments, then for each k: commitment_indices[k], cell_indices[k], coset_evals[k], proofs[k].

reachability.notes: Different serialization order would produce different challenge r values across clients, causing batch verification to produce different results.

property.severity_justification: Non-deterministic hash input ordering across clients produces different Fiat-Shamir challenges, causing consensus divergence on batch verification results for identical inputs.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating two clients that serialize the Fiat-Shamir hash input in different orders.

property.text: polynomial_eval_to_coeff (SG-007) MUST accept exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB evaluations as input. Inputs of any other length MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: The number of evaluations is derived from blob size. If blob_to_polynomial produces a non-standard number of evaluations, this invariant would be violated.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect evaluation count would produce polynomials of wrong degree, causing all subsequent KZG proof operations to be algebraically invalid.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires a code path where blob_to_polynomial returns non-FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB evaluations.

property.text: polynomial_eval_to_coeff (SG-007) MUST apply bit_reversal_permutation BEFORE the inverse FFT. Omitting or reordering this step produces incorrect coefficient representations that silently corrupt all KZG proofs.

reachability.notes: Every blob submitted triggers polynomial_eval_to_coeff. Incorrect bit-reversal ordering would produce wrong coefficients for all blobs processed by the affected client.

property.severity_justification: Bit-reversal permutation inconsistency between encoding (SG-007) and decoding (SG-023 recovery) paths causes all proofs generated by one client to fail verification on another, splitting the network.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires identifying a client where bit-reversal is applied in the wrong order or omitted.

property.text: add_polynomialcoeff (SG-008) MUST produce a result polynomial whose degree equals max(deg(a), deg(b)). The shorter polynomial MUST be zero-padded for missing coefficients, not truncated.

reachability.notes: Polynomial addition is a pure internal operation. Incorrectness would be an implementation bug.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect polynomial addition would propagate errors to interpolation and proof generation but requires an implementation bug to trigger.

property.text: multiply_polynomialcoeff (SG-009) MUST assert that len(a) + len(b) <= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB before computing the product. The product polynomial degree MUST equal deg(a) + deg(b).

reachability.notes: During recovery (SG-023), attacker-supplied cells determine the polynomial that is multiplied. If the degree bound assertion is missing, polynomials could exceed the trusted setup bounds.

property.severity_justification: Exceeding FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB degree bound would produce polynomials outside the trusted setup support, causing commitments to be computed with insufficient setup points, leading to incorrect or exploitable proofs.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a recovery scenario where the product polynomial exceeds the degree bound.

property.text: divide_polynomialcoeff (SG-010) MUST NOT accept a zero polynomial as the divisor b. If b is the zero polynomial, the function MUST reject the input with an error, never returning a result.

reachability.notes: The divisor is typically a vanishing polynomial computed from cell indices. A zero divisor would require all cell indices to be empty, which is blocked by the 50% threshold check.

property.severity_justification: Division by zero polynomial would cause a runtime crash. The 50% cell availability threshold should prevent this, but a missing check could lead to node crash.

property.text: divide_polynomialcoeff (SG-010) MUST ensure the leading coefficient of the divisor b[bpos] is nonzero. Division by a polynomial with a zero leading coefficient produces incorrect quotients.

reachability.notes: Vanishing polynomials are monic (leading coefficient 1) by construction, so this is a defensive check.

property.severity_justification: Monic vanishing polynomials guarantee a nonzero leading coefficient. Violation would require a bug in vanishing_polynomialcoeff.

property.text: interpolate_polynomialcoeff (SG-011) MUST require all x-values (xs) to be distinct. Duplicate x-values cause division by zero in the weight_adjustment computation (xs[i] - xs[j]).inverse(), which MUST crash or be explicitly rejected.

reachability.notes: During batch verification (SG-015), interpolation is performed over coset points derived from attacker-supplied cell_indices. If duplicate cell_indices are not rejected, duplicate x-values would reach interpolation.

property.severity_justification: Division by zero in field element inverse computation would crash the verifier node, causing denial of service. Alternatively, some implementations might return zero for a zero inverse, producing silently incorrect results.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC with duplicate cell_indices that bypass deduplication and reach interpolation.

property.text: For interpolate_polynomialcoeff (SG-011), the result polynomial MUST satisfy evaluate(result, xs[i]) == ys[i] for all i. The result degree MUST be at most len(xs) - 1.

reachability.notes: Lagrange interpolation correctness is a mathematical invariant. Violation indicates an implementation bug.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect interpolation would produce wrong commitment weights in batch verification, but requires an implementation bug.

property.text: vanishing_polynomialcoeff (SG-012) MUST produce a monic polynomial (leading coefficient 1) of degree exactly len(xs) that evaluates to 0 at every point in xs.

reachability.notes: Vanishing polynomial construction is algebraically determined. Violation would require a multiplication bug.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect vanishing polynomial would produce wrong quotient polynomials in KZG proof generation, corrupting proofs.
